articles.title: Lunar Shadows: How the Moon's Darkest Craters Could Host Lasers Ten Times More Stable Than Earth's
articles.summary: Permanently shadowed lunar craters offer an ultra-cold, ultra-high-vacuum environment that could boost laser stability to 10^-18—ten times better than Earth's best. This could revolutionize lunar navigation, gravitational wave detection, and dark matter searches. A prototype might reach the Moon within five years.

articles.title: From Zombie Fungi to Fossil Birds: The Living Tributes to David Attenborough on His 100th Birthday
articles.summary: Scientists have named roughly 50 organisms after David Attenborough, including a mind-controlling fungus and a toothless prehistoric bird. To mark his 100th birthday, we spotlight ten species that reflect his enduring influence on naturalists worldwide.

articles.title: Let It Cook: At Code with Claude, Developers Embrace AI That Codes, Tests, and Dreams
articles.summary: At Anthropic's developer conference, nearly half the attendees admitted to shipping AI-generated code without reading it. The company unveiled 'dreaming,' a feature that lets Claude learn from past tasks. But as automation accelerates, concerns about code quality and oversight are growing.
